name: Staphylococcus aureus
keyTest: Catalase (+), Coagulase (+), β-hemolytic, Mannitol salt agar (+)
tropism: Skin & Soft Tissue, Bone, Heart Valves
firstLineRx: Nafcillin / Oxacillin (MSSA) or Vancomycin (MRSA)
smear: Gram-positive spherical cocci arranged in irregular grape-like clusters.
culture: Golden-yellow pigment (staphyloxanthin) on sheep blood agar with prominent zone of beta-hemolysis; turns Mannitol Salt Agar bright yellow.
vignette: A 28-year-old person who injects drugs presents with persistent high fever, new tricuspid regurgitation murmur, and erythematous Janeway lesions on the palms.
virulence: Protein A binds IgG Fc region preventing opsonization; TSST-1 superantigen causes massive cytokine release (IL-1, IL-2, TNF-α); Exfoliatin A & B cause Scalded Skin Syndrome.
transmission: Direct contact, colonized anterior nares, IV catheter inoculation, surgical wounds.
buzzwords: Golden pigment, Janeway lesions & Osler nodes, Tricuspid endocarditis in IVDU, mecA gene encoding PBP2a.
chiefComplaint: A 28-year-old male presents with persistent high fever.

name: Streptococcus pneumoniae
keyTest: Catalase (-), Optochin sensitive, Bile soluble, α-hemolytic
firstLineRx: Amoxicillin / Ceftriaxone (or Vancomycin if high-level resistance)
smear: Gram-positive lancet-shaped paired cocci surrounded by clear unstained capsule halo on Gram stain.
culture: Alpha-hemolytic draftsman/umbilicated colonies with greenish hue on blood agar; growth inhibited by optochin (P-disk) and lysed by bile salts.
vignette: A 65-year-old male presents with abrupt onset of a single shaking chill, pleuritic chest pain, rust-colored sputum, and lobar consolidation on chest X-ray.
virulence: Polysaccharide capsule (major antigen & antiphagocytic); IgA protease cleaves secretory IgA; Pneumolysin damages ciliated epithelium.
transmission: Respiratory droplets; asplenic patients at high risk of fulminant encapsulated bacteremia.
buzzwords: Rusty sputum, Quellung reaction (+), Bile soluble, Lancet diplococci, #1 cause of community-acquired pneumonia and adult meningitis.
chiefComplaint: A 65-year-old male presents with sudden shaking chills.

name: Escherichia coli
keyTest: Lactose fermenter (pink MacConkey), Indole (+), Oxidase (-)
firstLineRx: Nitrofurantoin / TMP-SMX (Cystitis); Ceftriaxone (Pyelonephritis / Sepsis)
smear: Plump straight Gram-negative bacilli arranged singly or in loose pairs without capsule or spore formation.
culture: Rapid-growing bright pink colonies on MacConkey agar (vigorous lactose fermentation) and unmistakable iridescent green metallic sheen on EMB agar.
vignette: A 23-year-old woman experiences severe dysuria, increased urinary urgency, and suprapubic pain 48 hours after sexual intercourse, without flank tenderness.
virulence: P fimbriae mediate binding to uroepithelium (UTI); K1 capsular antigen resists phagocytosis (neonatal meningitis); Shiga-like toxin (EHEC O157:H7) causes HUS.
transmission: Ascending fecal flora, undercooked ground beef (EHEC), unpasteurized milk.
buzzwords: Green metallic sheen on EMB, P-fimbriae, K1 antigen, Hemolytic Uremic Syndrome (triad of hemolytic anemia, thrombocytopenia, acute renal failure).
chiefComplaint: A 23-year-old woman presents with severe dysuria.

name: Pseudomonas aeruginosa
keyTest: Oxidase (+), Non-lactose fermenter, Pyocyanin / Pyoverdine green pigment
tropism: Respiratory Tract, Skin & Soft Tissue, External Ear
firstLineRx: Cefepime / Piperacillin-tazobactam / Meropenem
smear: Slender Gram-negative rods with single polar flagellum exhibiting active darting motility.
culture: Non-lactose fermenting colonies (pale on MacConkey) with metallic sheen, diffusing vibrant blue-green pigments (pyocyanin) with distinct sweet grape-like / corn-tortilla odor.
vignette: A 16-year-old patient with cystic fibrosis presents with worsening chronic productive cough, green-tinted sputum, dyspnea, and bilateral bronchiectasis on CT.
virulence: Exotoxin A inactivate elongation factor 2 (EF-2) halting protein synthesis; Pyocyanin generates reactive oxygen species; Alginate slime biofilm in CF lungs.
transmission: Moist environmental reservoirs (water sinks, respirators, hot tubs, burn wounds).
buzzwords: Grape-like odor, Blue-green pyocyanin pigment, Ecthyma gangrenosum, Hot tub folliculitis, Malignant otitis externa in diabetics.
chiefComplaint: A 54-year-old burn patient develops foul-smelling wound discharge.

name: Neisseria meningitidis
keyTest: Maltose & Glucose fermenter, Oxidase (+), Thayer-Martin growth
firstLineRx: Ceftriaxone (Rifampin / Ciprofloxacin for household contacts prophylaxis)
smear: Intracellular and extracellular Gram-negative diplococci with adjacent flattened surfaces resembling opposing kidney beans.
culture: Enriched chocolate agar or selective Thayer-Martin / New York City medium; produces acid from both maltose and glucose; oxidase-positive.
vignette: An 18-year-old college student in a dormitory develops sudden severe headache, 39.5°C fever, photophobia, nuchal rigidity, and rapidly spreading petechial purpura on trunk and extremities.
virulence: Lipooligosaccharide (LOS) endotoxin triggers severe septic shock and DIC; IgA protease degrades mucosal immunity; Polysaccharide capsule (A, B, C, Y, W-135).
transmission: Respiratory droplets in crowded living conditions (military barracks, dormitories).
buzzwords: Petechial rash, Waterhouse-Friderichsen syndrome (adrenal hemorrhage), Ferments Maltose & Glucose (vs Gonococcus which ferments Glucose only).
chiefComplaint: An 18-year-old college student develops sudden severe headache.

name: Clostridioides difficile
keyTest: Stool Toxin A & B EIA / PCR, CCFA agar growth
firstLineRx: Oral Vancomycin or Fidaxomicin
smear: Gram-positive straight rods displaying subterminal oval endospores under anaerobic cultivation.
culture: Cycloserine-cefoxitin-fructose agar (CCFA) strictly under anaerobic conditions, showing flat yellow colonies with horse-dung odor and yellow-green fluorescence under UV light.
vignette: A 72-year-old hospitalized patient treated 10 days prior with clindamycin for pneumonia develops watery diarrhea (12 bowel movements/day), abdominal cramping, and yellow raised pseudomembranes on sigmoidoscopy.
virulence: Toxin A (enterotoxin) binds brush border causing mucosal inflammation; Toxin B (cytotoxin) disrupts actin cytoskeleton via UDP-glucose glucosylation causing pseudomembranes.
transmission: Fecal-oral ingestion of heat/acid-resistant spores in healthcare settings; soap and water required for hand hygiene.
buzzwords: Pseudomembranous colitis, Clindamycin / Fluoroquinolone exposure, Megacolon, Spores resistant to alcohol rubs.
chiefComplaint: A 72-year-old hospitalized patient develops profuse watery diarrhea.

name: Mycobacterium tuberculosis
keyTest: Ziehl-Neelsen / Kinyoun (+), Niacin (+), Lowenstein-Jensen growth
firstLineRx: Rifampin + Isoniazid + Pyrazinamide + Ethambutol (RIPE regimen)
smear: Slender, slightly curved or beaded red/fuchsia rods resisting acid alcohol decolonization on Ziehl-Neelsen / Kinyoun carbolfuchsin staining.
culture: Extremely slow growth (3 to 6 weeks) on Lowenstein-Jensen or Middlebrook medium yielding rough, crumbly, buff/cream 'breadcrumb' colonies with serpentine cord factor.
vignette: A 48-year-old man presents with 2 months of low-grade afternoon fevers, drenching night sweats, 20-pound unintentional weight loss, hemoptysis, and apical cavitary infiltrates on chest radiograph.
virulence: Cord factor (trehalose 6,6'-dimycolate) inhibits macrophage maturation; Sulfatides prevent phagolysosome fusion; Catalase-peroxidase (KatG) activates isoniazid.
transmission: Inhalation of airborne droplet nuclei into pulmonary alveoli; survives inside unactivated macrophages.
buzzwords: Caseating granulomas, Langhans giant cells, Ghon complex, Apical cavitations, Pott disease (spine), Night sweats & hemoptysis.
chiefComplaint: A 48-year-old man presents with chronic afternoon fevers.

name: Yersinia pestis
keyTest: Wayson / Giemsa bipolar staining, Non-motile at 37°C, Oxidase (-)
firstLineRx: Gentamicin or Streptomycin / Doxycycline
smear: Small pleomorphic Gram-negative coccobacilli with rounded ends exhibiting distinct bipolar safety-pin staining with Wayson or Giemsa dye.
culture: Slow growth on blood agar; colonies exhibit characteristic hammered-metal or fried-egg appearance at 48 hours; produces stalactite growth in nutrient broth with oil droplet.
vignette: A hiker in Arizona develops sudden high fever, chills, profound prostration, and an exquisitely tender, golf-ball-sized fluctuant inguinal lymph node after flea bites from wild rodents.
virulence: Yop proteins (Type III secretion system) disrupt host macrophage signaling; F1 capsular antigen prevents phagocytosis; Endotoxin induces gangrene and acral necrosis.
transmission: Bite of Xenopsylla cheopis flea from rodent reservoirs (prairie dogs, ground squirrels) or aerosol droplets in pneumonic plague.
buzzwords: Safety-pin bipolar staining, Suppurative buboes, Acral gangrene ('Black Death'), Four Corners region of US.
chiefComplaint: A 34-year-old hiker develops sudden high fever.

name: Listeria monocytogenes
keyTest: Tumbling motility at 22-25°C, CAMP test (+), Esculin hydrolysis (+)
firstLineRx: Ampicillin (+/- Gentamicin for synergy)
smear: Small, regular Gram-positive rods or coccobacilli in pairs or short chains, frequently confused with Corynebacterium or Streptococcus.
culture: Narrow zone of beta-hemolysis on sheep blood agar resembling Group B Strep; exhibits characteristic tumbling motility in wet mount at room temperature and umbrella motility in semisolid agar.
vignette: A pregnant woman in her 32nd week eats unpasteurized soft cheese and develops febrile gastroenteritis; CSF analysis of her septic newborn reveals Gram-positive rods with tumbling motility.
virulence: Listeriolysin O forms pores in phagosomal membrane allowing intracellular escape; ActA polymerizes host actin rocket tails for cell-to-cell spread.
transmission: Ingestion of unpasteurized milk/cheese, cold cuts, deli meats; can multiply at refrigeration temperatures (4°C cold enrichment).
buzzwords: Actin rockets, Tumbling motility, Cold enrichment (survives in fridge), Granulomatosis infantiseptica in neonates.
chiefComplaint: A 29-year-old pregnant woman develops mild flu-like illness.

name: Cryptococcus neoformans
keyTest: India Ink (+), Cryptococcal antigen (CrAg) LFA (+), Urease (+)
firstLineRx: Amphotericin B + Flucytosine induction, followed by Fluconazole maintenance
smear: India ink wet mount of CSF shows round-to-oval yeasts with narrow-based budding surrounded by wide translucent halo of thick polysaccharide capsule.
culture: Mucoid, creamy white-to-tan colonies on Sabouraud dextrose agar; produces dark brown/black melanin pigment on caffeic acid / birdseed agar; urease positive.
vignette: An individual with untreated HIV and a CD4 count of 35 cells/µL presents with progressive subacute dull headache, malaise, low-grade fever, neck stiffness, and papilledema.
virulence: Glucuronoxylomannan (GXM) polysaccharide capsule (heavily antiphagocytic); Phenol oxidase produces melanin protecting yeast from free radicals.
transmission: Inhalation of soil enriched with pigeon droppings; opportunistic pathogen primarily in immunocompromised (CD4 < 100).
buzzwords: Soap bubble lesions in basal ganglia, Mucicarmine stain (red capsule), India ink halo, Pigeon droppings, Narrow-based budding.
chiefComplaint: A 38-year-old immunocompromised patient presents with progressive subacute headache.

name: Treponema pallidum
keyTest: Darkfield microscopy, RPR/VDRL screening, FTA-ABS / TP-PA confirmation
tropism: Genital Tract, Skin & Soft Tissue, CNS, Cardiovascular
firstLineRx: Benzathine Penicillin G (intramuscular depot)
smear: Cannot be seen on standard light microscopy with Gram stain; darkfield microscopy demonstrates thin, delicate, tightly coiled helical spirochetes with corkscrew motility.
culture: Cannot be cultivated on artificial cell-free laboratory culture media; relies on serologic assays or rabbit testicular passage.
vignette: A 26-year-old male presents with a solitary, indurated, completely painless ulcer on his coronal sulcus and non-tender bilateral rubbery inguinal adenopathy.
virulence: Hyaluronidase facilitates tissue penetration; Endoflagella enclosed within periplasmic space provide motility through dense mucus; Antigenic masking avoids immune surveillance.
transmission: Sexual contact (primary mucosal abrasion) or transplacental transmission (congenital syphilis).
buzzwords: Painless hard chancre, Tabes dorsalis (neurosyphilis), Argyll Robertson pupil (accommodates but doesn't react to light), VDRL/RPR false positives (lupus/antiphospholipid).
chiefComplaint: A 26-year-old male presents with a single painless genital ulcer.

name: Vibrio cholerae
keyTest: TCBS agar yellow colonies, Oxidase (+), Darting / shooting motility
firstLineRx: Aggressive Oral/IV Rehydration Solution + Doxycycline / Azithromycin
smear: Short, curved, comma-shaped Gram-negative bacilli demonstrating rapid darting motility reminiscent of shooting stars.
culture: Thiosulfate-citrate-bile salts-sucrose (TCBS) agar produces large yellow sucrose-fermenting colonies; grows well in alkaline peptone water (pH 8.6).
vignette: Following clean water disruption after an earthquake, a 35-year-old relief worker experiences sudden explosive painless diarrhea resembling cloudy rice water with washerwoman hands and hypotension.
virulence: Cholera toxin (AB5 toxin) constitutively ADP-ribosylates Gs alpha, permanently activating adenylate cyclase & raising cAMP, causing massive secretomotor Cl- and water efflux.
transmission: Fecal-oral ingestion of contaminated water or seafood; sensitive to stomach acid (high infectious dose required unless achlorhydric).
buzzwords: Rice-water stool, Permanent Gs activation via ADP-ribosylation, TCBS yellow colonies, Profuse painless secretory diarrhea.
chiefComplaint: A 35-year-old relief worker develops sudden explosive watery diarrhea.

name: Bacillus anthracis
keyTest: Non-motile, Non-hemolytic, Poly-D-glutamate capsule, 'Medusa-head' colonies
firstLineRx: Ciprofloxacin or Doxycycline + Clindamycin/Rifampin
smear: Long chains of large, square-ended, blunt Gram-positive bacilli ('boxcar' rods) with prominent clear spores when exposed to air.
culture: Non-hemolytic, tenacious, gray-white colonies on blood agar with irregular comma-shaped border projections resembling a 'Medusa head'; stands up like beaten egg white.
vignette: A tanner handling imported goat hides presents with a painless itchy papule on his forearm that developed vesicles and transformed into a depressed black eschar surrounded by brawny edema.
virulence: Poly-D-glutamic acid capsule (polypeptide, not polysaccharide); Anthrax toxin composed of Protective Antigen (PA), Edema Factor (EF, adenylate cyclase), and Lethal Factor (LF, zinc metalloprotease).
transmission: Contact with infected animal hides/wool (Woolsorter's disease), spore inhalation, or bioterrorism.
buzzwords: Black necrotic eschar, Widened mediastinum on CXR (hemorrhagic mediastinitis), Poly-D-glutamate capsule, Medusa-head colonies.
chiefComplaint: A 42-year-old leather tanner presents with a painless black skin ulcer.

name: Legionella pneumophila
keyTest: BCYE agar required (Cysteine & Iron), Urinary Antigen Test (+)
firstLineRx: Levofloxacin / Moxifloxacin or Azithromycin
smear: Faintly staining, pleomorphic Gram-negative bacilli that stain poorly on routine Gram stain; silver impregnation (Dieterle stain) required.
culture: Fails to grow on standard blood or chocolate agar; requires Buffered Charcoal Yeast Extract (BCYE) agar supplemented with L-cysteine and iron; shows iridescent 'ground-glass' colonies.
vignette: A 56-year-old executive attending a hotel convention with air-conditioning cooling towers develops high fever, watery non-bloody diarrhea, confusion, hyponatremia (126 mEq/L), and dense lobar pneumonia.
virulence: Type IVB secretion system (Dot/Icm) manipulates host cell vacuolar transport, replicating inside alveolar macrophage phagosomes.
transmission: Aerosols from contaminated warm water systems (cooling towers, hotel air conditioning, cruise ships, whirlpool spas); no person-to-person spread.
buzzwords: Atypical pneumonia + Diarrhea + Hyponatremia + Confusion, BCYE charcoal agar (iron and cysteine), Urinary antigen test.
chiefComplaint: A 56-year-old executive presents with high remittent fever.

name: Streptococcus pyogenes
keyTest: Catalase (-), Bacitracin sensitive (A-disk), PYR (+), β-hemolytic
firstLineRx: Penicillin V / Amoxicillin (Cephalexin or Clindamycin if penicillin allergy)
smear: Gram-positive spherical to ovoid cocci arranged in pairs and prominent long tandem chains.
culture: Small translucent colonies surrounded by wide, sharp, clear zones of complete beta-hemolysis on sheep blood agar; growth inhibited by low-dose bacitracin disk; PYR positive.
vignette: A 7-year-old child presents with sudden severe throat pain, 39°C fever, tonsillopharyngeal erythema with white exudates, palatal petechiae, and tender anterior cervical lymphadenitis without rhinorrhea or cough.
virulence: M protein prevents complement activation and opsonization (molecular mimicry induces Rheumatic Fever); Streptolysin O/S lyses RBCs; Pyrogenic exotoxins (SpeA/C) cause Scarlet Fever / STSS.
transmission: Respiratory droplets, direct contact with skin lesions (impetigo, erysipelas).
buzzwords: M protein molecular mimicry, Bacitracin sensitive (A-disk), PYR positive, Scarlet fever strawberry tongue & sandpaper rash, Rheumatic fever (Jones criteria).
chiefComplaint: A 7-year-old child presents with sudden severe throat pain.

name: Haemophilus influenzae
keyTest: Requires Factor X (hemin) & V (NAD), Satellite phenomenon around S. aureus
firstLineRx: Ceftriaxone (Meningitis/Epiglottitis); Amoxicillin-clavulanate (Otitis/Sinusitis)
smear: Small, pleomorphic, faintly counterstaining Gram-negative coccobacilli that can resemble diplococci or short bacilli.
culture: Does not grow on 5% sheep blood agar unless near S. aureus colonies (satellitism, supplying factor V); grows luxuriantly on chocolate agar providing both Factor X (hemin) and Factor V (NAD).
vignette: An unimmunized 3-year-old child presents with high fever, severe inspiratory stridor, drooling while sitting leaning forward in a tripod position; lateral neck X-ray reveals 'thumbprint' sign.
virulence: Polyribosylribitol phosphate (PRP) capsule (Type b) invasive antiphagocytic; IgA protease mucosal colonizer; endotoxin LOS causes inflammation.
transmission: Respiratory droplets; dramatically reduced incidence of Type b invasive disease with PRP conjugate vaccine.
buzzwords: Thumbprint sign on lateral neck X-ray, Cherry red epiglottitis, Satellite test with S. aureus, Chocolate agar with Factor X and V.
chiefComplaint: An unimmunized 3-year-old child presents with inspiratory stridor.

name: Salmonella enterica (Typhi)
keyTest: Non-lactose fermenter, H2S production (black colonies on Hektoen), Motile
firstLineRx: Ceftriaxone or Ciprofloxacin / Azithromycin
smear: Gram-negative, motile bacilli with peritrichous flagella without visible spore or capsule.
culture: Non-lactose fermenter (colorless on MacConkey agar); produces hydrogen sulfide (H2S), yielding colonies with prominent jet-black centers on Hektoen enteric and Salmonella-Shigella (SS) agars.
vignette: A traveler returning from South Asia presents with 10 days of step-ladder fever, relative bradycardia (Faget sign), faint blanching salmon-pink rose spots on the abdomen, and hepatosplenomegaly.
virulence: Vi capsular antigen protects against antibody and complement; survives in macrophages of reticuloendothelial system; chronic colonizer in biliary gallbladder.
transmission: Fecal-oral route via contaminated food or water; asymptomatic chronic carriers (e.g. Typhoid Mary).
buzzwords: Rose spots on trunk, Relative bradycardia (Faget sign), Black colonies on Hektoen (H2S+), Chronic carrier state in gallbladder, Peyer patch necrosis.
chiefComplaint: A 29-year-old traveler presents with prolonged step-ladder fever.

name: Campylobacter jejuni
keyTest: Grows at 42°C on Campy-BAP, Oxidase (+), Catalase (+)
firstLineRx: Azithromycin (or supportive hydration for mild cases)
smear: Faintly staining, slender Gram-negative curved rods resembling seagull wings or spiral S-shapes with single polar flagellum.
culture: Microaerophilic (5% O2, 10% CO2); requires selective antibiotic-containing medium (Campy-BAP / Skirrow) and elevated thermophilic temperature (42°C).
vignette: A 21-year-old college student who ate undercooked barbecue chicken develops severe periumbilical cramping mimicking appendicitis, fever, and 8 episodes of bloody loose diarrhea per day.
virulence: Cytolethal distending toxin (CDT) causes DNA damage and cell cycle arrest; molecular mimicry between LOS and host gangliosides (GM1) triggers Guillain-Barré syndrome.
transmission: Undercooked poultry, unpasteurized milk, contaminated water, contact with infected domestic puppies.
buzzwords: Seagull-wing shaped, Grows at 42°C ('Campers like hot campfires'), Guillain-Barré syndrome (ascending paralysis), Reactive arthritis.
chiefComplaint: A 21-year-old college student develops severe cramping bloody diarrhea.

name: Dengue virus
keyTest: NS1 Antigen ELISA, RT-PCR, Tourniquet test (+), Severe Thrombocytopenia
firstLineRx: Supportive hydration (judicious IV fluids), Acetaminophen (Avoid NSAIDs/Aspirin)
smear: Viruses cannot be resolved on standard light microscopy; electron microscopy demonstrates spherical enveloped virions (~50 nm) with icosahedral capsid symmetry.
culture: Cultured in mosquito cell lines (C6/36) or Vero cells; diagnosed clinically via NS1 viral antigen capture or serum RT-PCR in early acute phase.
vignette: A 24-year-old traveler returning from Southeast Asia presents with severe retro-orbital headache, 40°C saddleback fever, severe generalized arthralgia and myalgia ('breakbone fever'), petechiae upon blood pressure cuff inflation, and platelet count of 42,000/µL.
virulence: Antibody-dependent enhancement (ADE) by sub-neutralizing heterotypic antibodies from prior infection promotes severe Dengue Hemorrhagic Fever / Shock Syndrome; NS1 causes capillary leak.
transmission: Bite of diurnal Aedes aegypti / Aedes albopictus mosquitoes.
buzzwords: Breakbone fever, Retro-orbital pain, Tourniquet test (+), Aedes mosquito, Antibody-dependent enhancement (ADE), Plasma leak.
chiefComplaint: A 24-year-old traveler presents with severe retro-orbital pain.

name: Rabies lyssavirus
keyTest: Negri bodies (eosinophilic cytoplasmic inclusions), RT-PCR of saliva/nuchal skin, Direct fluorescent antibody (DFA)
tropism: Peripheral Nerves, CNS (Limbic system / Hippocampus / Purkinje cells), Salivary Glands
firstLineRx: Post-exposure prophylaxis: Rabies Immunoglobulin (HRIG) wound infiltration + 4-dose Inactivated Vaccine (days 0, 3, 7, 14)
smear: Histopathology reveals pathognomonic round, eosinophilic cytoplasmic Negri inclusion bodies in cerebellar Purkinje cells and hippocampal pyramidal neurons.
culture: Confirmed via direct fluorescent antibody (DFA) testing on frozen brain tissue or reverse-transcriptase PCR of saliva or full-thickness nuchal skin biopsy.
vignette: A 32-year-old caver presents with agitation, autonomic instability, excruciating pharyngeal spasms triggered by trying to drink a glass of water (hydrophobia), hypersalivation, and bizarre behavior 6 weeks after waking with a bat in the bedroom.
virulence: Glycoprotein G binds nicotinic acetylcholine receptors (nAChR) at neuromuscular junction; travels by retrograde axonal transport along peripheral nerves (dynein motor) into dorsal root ganglia and CNS.
transmission: Bite or scratch from infected animals (bats #1 in USA, dogs #1 worldwide, raccoons, skunks, foxes).
buzzwords: Bullet-shaped virion, Negri bodies in Purkinje cells, Hydrophobia & aerophobia, Retrograde dynein axonal transport, 100% case fatality once symptoms appear.
chiefComplaint: A 32-year-old caver presents with excruciating throat spasms when swallowing water.

name: Human immunodeficiency virus 1
keyTest: 4th gen HIV-1/2 Antigen/Antibody combination immunoassay (p24), Confirmatory differentiation assay, Quantitative HIV-RNA PCR
tropism: Immune System (CD4+ T Cells, Macrophages, Dendritic cells)
firstLineRx: Combination Antiretroviral Therapy (cART): 2 NRTIs (e.g. Tenofovir + Emtricitabine) + 1 INSTI (e.g. Bictegravir / Dolutegravir)
smear: Electron microscopy reveals spherical enveloped virion containing unique truncated cone-shaped capsid core composed of p24 major capsid protein.
culture: Screened with 4th generation antigen/antibody combo immunoassay detecting both p24 capsid antigen and anti-HIV IgM/IgG; viral load quantified by real-time RT-PCR.
vignette: A 34-year-old male presents with persistent oral candidiasis, chronic diarrhea, 15-pound weight loss, and diffuse lymphadenopathy; laboratory workup reveals CD4+ count of 140 cells/µL.
virulence: gp120 binds CD4 and chemokine co-receptors (CCR5 for macrophage-tropic, CXCR4 for T-cell-tropic); gp41 mediates viral membrane fusion; reverse transcriptase lacks proofreading leading to rapid mutational escape.
transmission: Sexual contact, parenteral inoculation (blood transfusion, shared IV needles), vertical transmission (transplacental, intrapartum, breastfeeding).
buzzwords: gp120 / gp41, p24 capsid antigen, CCR5 mutation (homozygous Δ32 confers resistance), Opportunistic infections when CD4 < 200, Retroviral diploid RNA.
chiefComplaint: A 34-year-old male presents with chronic unexplained weight loss.

name: Influenza A virus
keyTest: Rapid molecular NAAT / RT-PCR, Rapid Influenza Diagnostic Antigen Test (RIDT)
firstLineRx: Oseltamivir (oral neuraminidase inhibitor) or Baloxavir marboxil (cap-dependent endonuclease inhibitor)
smear: Enveloped helical nucleocapsid virus possessing 8 negative-sense, single-stranded RNA gene segments studded with hemagglutinin and neuraminidase glycoprotein spikes.
culture: Propagated in embryonated chicken eggs or Madin-Darby canine kidney (MDCK) cells; diagnostic confirmation achieved within hours via multiplex respiratory PCR panel.
vignette: In January, a 42-year-old schoolteacher presents with sudden onset of 39.4°C fever, severe diffuse body myalgias, prominent retrosternal burning chest pain, non-productive cough, and prostration.
virulence: Hemagglutinin (HA) binds sialic acid receptors promoting viral endocytosis; Neuraminidase (NA) cleaves sialic acid to release progeny virions; Antigenic drift (point mutations) causes seasonal epidemics; Antigenic shift (segment reassortment) causes global pandemics.
transmission: Respiratory droplets and contaminated fomites; secondary bacterial superinfection with S. aureus or S. pneumoniae can cause fatal pneumonia.
buzzwords: 8 RNA segments, Hemagglutinin & Neuraminidase, Antigenic drift (mutations) vs Shift (reassortment), Secondary S. aureus pneumonia, Oseltamivir.
chiefComplaint: A 42-year-old schoolteacher presents with abrupt onset of high fever.

name: Herpes simplex virus 1
keyTest: CSF / Lesion PCR, Tzanck smear (multinucleated giant cells), Cowdry A intranuclear inclusions
tropism: Oral Mucosa, Trigeminal Ganglia (Latency), Temporal Lobes (Encephalitis)
firstLineRx: Oral / IV Acyclovir or Valacyclovir
smear: Tzanck prep of unroofed vesicle base demonstrates multinucleated giant cells with molding and ground-glass nuclei containing eosinophilic Cowdry A intranuclear inclusion bodies.
culture: Rapid cytopathic effect on human diploid fibroblast monolayers showing ballooning degeneration; PCR is gold standard for CSF and mucocutaneous specimens.
vignette: A 50-year-old woman develops fever, olfactory hallucinations, bizarre behavioral changes, and focal seizures; brain MRI shows hyperintensity restricted to the left frontotemporal lobe, and CSF PCR is diagnostic.
virulence: Enters latency in sensory nerve ganglia (trigeminal ganglia for HSV-1); reactivated by physical or emotional stress, fever, UV light, or immunosuppression; downregulates MHC Class I expression.
transmission: Direct contact with infectious saliva or vesicular fluid (cold sores, gingivostomatitis, keratoconjunctivitis).
buzzwords: Temporal lobe encephalitis, Cowdry A inclusion bodies, Tzanck smear multinucleated giant cells, Trigeminal ganglion latency, Gingivostomatitis.
chiefComplaint: A 50-year-old woman develops acute temporal lobe seizures.

name: Respiratory syncytial virus
keyTest: Multiplex respiratory viral PCR panel, Rapid antigen detection
firstLineRx: Supportive oxygenation & hydration (Palivizumab monoclonal antibody prophylaxis for premature infants; Nirsevimab; Ribavirin for severe SCID)
smear: Enveloped single-stranded negative-sense RNA virus expressing surface Fusion (F) protein and Glycoprotein (G).
culture: Inoculation in tissue culture leads to characteristic syncytia formation (large multinucleated giant cells from cell-to-cell fusion).
vignette: A 3-month-old infant in winter presents with low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, severe wheezing, tachypnea (68 breaths/min), and intercostal retractions; CXR shows hyperinflation with peribronchial cuffing.
virulence: Fusion (F) protein induces syncytium formation causing mucosal sloughing, epithelial necrosis, and micro-plugging of infant bronchioles with mucus and fibrin.
transmission: Respiratory droplets and fomites in daycare centers; #1 cause of fatal bronchiolitis and pneumonia in infants under 1 year of age.
buzzwords: F protein syncytia formation, #1 cause of bronchiolitis in infants, Palivizumab monoclonal antibody, Winter epidemics, Hyperinflation on chest radiograph.
chiefComplaint: A 3-month-old infant presents with severe audible wheezing.

name: Plasmodium falciparum
keyTest: Giemsa-stained thin & thick blood smears, Rapid Antigen Test (BinaxNOW / PfHRP2)
tropism: Bloodstream (Erythrocytes of all ages), Liver (Schizogony), Brain Microvasculature
firstLineRx: Artemisinin-based combination therapy (ACT, e.g. Artemether-lumefantrine) or IV Artesunate for severe malaria
smear: Giemsa-stained peripheral blood smear reveals multiple delicate ring-form trophozoites within single non-enlarged RBCs and diagnostic crescent / banana-shaped gametocytes; Maurer clefts present.
culture: Diagnosed directly from whole-blood microscopy or PfHRP2/aldolase rapid lateral flow antigen strip; artificial culture requires specialized microaerophilic RPMI red cell medium.
vignette: A 31-year-old traveler returning from Nigeria develops irregular cyclic fever, drenching sweats, dark urine ('blackwater fever'), confusion, and severe hemolytic anemia with parasitemia of 8%.
virulence: PfEMP1 (Plasmodium falciparum erythrocyte membrane protein 1) on erythrocyte surface knobs binds ICAM-1 and CD36 on microvascular endothelium causing cytoadherence and microvascular occlusion (cerebral malaria).
transmission: Bite of nocturnal female Anopheles mosquito; blood transfusion; congenital transmission.
buzzwords: Banana/crescent-shaped gametocytes, Multiple rings per RBC, Cerebral malaria, Blackwater fever, Sickle cell trait (HbAS) confers resistance.
chiefComplaint: A 31-year-old traveler develops cyclic shaking fevers.

name: Giardia lamblia (duodenalis)
keyTest: Stool Ova & Parasite (O&P) exam, Stool Giardia antigen EIA / NAAT
firstLineRx: Metronidazole or Tinidazole / Nitazoxanide
smear: Stool smear wet mount shows pear-shaped, dorsally convex trophozoites with two nuclei resembling 'spectacles' or 'smiling face' and four pairs of flagella exhibiting characteristic falling-leaf motility; oval quadrinucleated cysts in formed stool.
culture: Not routinely cultured; diagnosed via fecal ELISA antigen detection or microscopic demonstration of cysts and trophozoites in stool or duodenal aspirate.
vignette: A 27-year-old backpacker who drank untreated mountain stream water on a Rocky Mountain hiking trip develops foul-smelling, greasy floating stools (steatorrhea), sulfurous burps, abdominal distension, and weight loss 2 weeks later.
virulence: Ventral concave adhesive suction disk attaches tightly to duodenal brush border enterocytes, producing mechanical villous blunting and malabsorption without tissue invasion.
transmission: Fecal-oral ingestion of chlorination-resistant cysts from contaminated stream water or daycares; common in campers and beaver habitats.
buzzwords: Falling leaf motility, Smiling face / spectacles binucleated trophozoite, Greasy foul-smelling steatorrhea, Beaver fever, IgA deficiency predisposes to chronic infection.
chiefComplaint: A 27-year-old backpacker develops foul-smelling greasy diarrhea.

name: Entamoeba histolytica
keyTest: Stool E. histolytica antigen / PCR, Stool microscopy for erythrophagocytosis, Serum amebic serology
tropism: GI Tract (Cecum & Colon), Liver (Right Lobe Abscess)
firstLineRx: Metronidazole or Tinidazole (tissue amebicide) followed by Paromomycin or Iodoquinol (luminal cysticide)
smear: Fresh stool warm saline wet mount reveals active amoeboid trophozoites with single spherical nucleus containing central pinpoint karyosome and pathognomonic engulfed red blood cells (erythrophagocytosis).
culture: Diagnostic amebic stool antigen ELISA or PCR differentiates pathogenic E. histolytica from non-pathogenic E. dispar; liver aspirate reveals odorless thick reddish-brown fluid.
vignette: A 39-year-old immigrant from Central America presents with right upper quadrant abdominal pain, fever, weight loss, and an 8-cm solitary hypoechoic cyst in the right hepatic lobe; liver aspiration yields 'anchovy-paste' exudate.
virulence: Gal/GalNAc lectin mediates adherence to colonic mucin and host enterocytes; Amoebapore peptides create holes in host membranes causing cell lysis; cysteine proteases degrade extracellular matrix producing flask-shaped ulcers.
transmission: Fecal-oral ingestion of infectious 4-nucleated mature cysts in fecally contaminated food or water.
buzzwords: Flask-shaped intestinal ulcers, Anchovy paste liver abscess, Erythrophagocytosis (RBCs inside amoeba), Luminal cysticide required (Paromomycin).
chiefComplaint: A 39-year-old man presents with right upper quadrant abdominal pain.

name: Toxoplasma gondii
keyTest: Brain MRI (Multiple ring-enhancing lesions), Toxoplasma IgG/IgM serology, Biopsy demonstrating tachyzoites
tropism: CNS (Basal Ganglia), Retina, Skeletal & Cardiac Muscle
firstLineRx: Sulfadiazine + Pyrimethamine (supplemented with Leucovorin / folinic acid)
smear: Giemsa or Wright-stained biopsy shows crescent-shaped tachyzoites (rapidly dividing form) with pointed anterior end or dormant pseudocysts packed with bradyzoites.
culture: Confirmed through serologic testing, real-time PCR of CSF/amniotic fluid, or characteristic radiographic imaging; mice inoculation used in reference labs.
vignette: An HIV patient with CD4 count of 45 cells/µL presents with progressive focal left-sided hemiparesis and new-onset seizures; head MRI reveals multiple bilateral ring-enhancing lesions with surrounding edema in the basal ganglia.
virulence: Invasive microneme and rhoptry proteins discharge to construct a protective parasitophorous vacuole avoiding phagolysosome degradation; latent bradyzoite tissue cysts reactivate during cellular immunosuppression.
transmission: Ingestion of oocysts from domestic cat feces (litter box) or tissue cysts in undercooked pork/lamb; transplacental transmission causes congenital toxoplasmosis.
buzzwords: Multiple ring-enhancing lesions on brain MRI, Cat feces / litter box, Congenital triad (chorioretinitis, hydrocephalus, intracranial calcifications), Pyrimethamine + Sulfadiazine.
chiefComplaint: A 41-year-old immunocompromised patient develops progressive unilateral limb weakness.

name: Leptospira interrogans
keyTest: Microscopic Agglutination Test (MAT), Leptospira PCR, Darkfield microscopy
firstLineRx: Doxycycline (mild); IV Penicillin G or Ceftriaxone (severe Weil disease)
smear: Very thin, delicate, tightly coiled spirochetes with characteristic hooked ends resembling question marks or ice-tongs visible on darkfield microscopy or silver impregnation stain.
culture: Grows slowly (takes weeks) in specialized protein-rich Fletcher or EMJH semisolid media; routinely diagnosed via serology (MAT) or serum/urine PCR.
vignette: A triathlete who competed in freshwater river kayaking in Hawaii presents with high fever, intense calf muscle tenderness, jaundice, elevated creatinine (acute kidney injury), and prominent bilateral conjunctival suffusion without purulent discharge.
virulence: Outer membrane proteins (LipL32, OmpL1) facilitate rapid burrowing through abraded skin and intact mucous membranes; hemolysins cause capillary endothelial injury and hemorrhage.
transmission: Exposure of broken skin or mucosal membranes to freshwater, mud, or soil contaminated with urine of infected rodents or domestic livestock.
buzzwords: Conjunctival suffusion without exudate, Hooked ends like question mark / ice tongs, Severe calf tenderness, Weil disease (triad: jaundice, renal failure, hemorrhage), Freshwater kayaking / surfing in Hawaii.
chiefComplaint: A 29-year-old triathlete presents with intense calf muscle tenderness.

name: Borrelia burgdorferi
keyTest: Two-tier serology (Enzyme Immunoassay screen + Western blot confirmation)
tropism: Skin, Joints (Large joints / Knee), Cardiovascular (AV block), CNS (Facial nerve)
firstLineRx: Doxycycline (Amoxicillin in pregnant women and young children; IV Ceftriaxone for heart block/neuroborreliosis)
smear: Unlike Treponema, Borrelia is larger and can be visualized under light microscopy using Giemsa or Wright aniline stains as loosely coiled, flexible spiral micro-organisms.
culture: Barbour-Stoenner-Kelly (BSK) liquid medium under microaerophilic conditions; clinical diagnosis relies predominantly on two-tiered serologic antibody testing.
vignette: A 35-year-old gardener in Connecticut presents in summer with a growing, painless 12-cm annular erythematous rash with central clearing ('bull's-eye') on his thigh, accompanied by flu-like fatigue and headache.
virulence: OspA and OspC surface lipoproteins mediate adherence within tick midgut and migration to salivary gland; antigenic variation of VlsE surface protein allows chronic immune evasion.
transmission: Bite of Ixodes scapularis / pacificus deer tick (must feed for >36–48 hours for spirochete transmission); white-footed mouse is primary reservoir, white-tailed deer is obligate mating host.
buzzwords: Erythema migrans (bull's-eye rash), Ixodes deer tick, Bilateral facial nerve palsy (Bell palsy), Third-degree AV heart block, Migratory asymmetric monoarthritis of the knee.
chiefComplaint: A 35-year-old gardener presents with an expanding annular red rash.

name: Mycoplasma pneumoniae
keyTest: Cold Agglutinins titer (IgM), Respiratory PCR, 'Fried-egg' colonies on Eaton agar
firstLineRx: Macrolides (Azithromycin) or Doxycycline / Respiratory Fluoroquinolones (Inherent resistance to beta-lactams!)
smear: Lacks peptidoglycan cell wall completely; enclosed only by single sterol-containing lipid trilaminar membrane; not visible on Gram stain.
culture: Eaton agar supplemented with cholesterol; extremely slow growth showing tiny microscopic 'fried-egg' colonies with dense central core; diagnosed clinically by PCR or cold agglutinin titer.
vignette: A 19-year-old military recruit develops insidious dry hacking cough, low-grade fever, sore throat, and bullous myringitis; chest X-ray looks dramatically worse than the patient appears, revealing diffuse bilateral interstitial infiltrates.
virulence: P1 cytoadhesin binds sialic acid receptors at base of respiratory cilia, inhibiting ciliary clearance; Community-Acquired Respiratory Distress Syndrome (CARDS) toxin causes mucosal vacuolation.
transmission: Respiratory droplets in close contact settings (military barracks, boarding schools, college dormitories).
buzzwords: No cell wall (resistant to penicillins/cephalosporins), Cold agglutinins (IgM causes hemolytic anemia), Bullous myringitis, Eaton agar fried-egg colonies, CXR looks worse than patient.
chiefComplaint: A 19-year-old military recruit develops an insidious dry hacking cough.

name: Chlamydia trachomatis
keyTest: Nucleic Acid Amplification Test (NAAT), Giemsa stain (intracytoplasmic inclusions)
firstLineRx: Doxycycline (100 mg BID x 7 days) or single-dose Azithromycin (plus Ceftriaxone to co-treat Gonorrhea)
smear: Gram stain reveals polymorphonuclear leukocytes (pus cells) without visible bacteria; Giemsa stain or direct fluorescent antibody reveals glycogen-rich perinuclear cytoplasmic inclusion bodies.
culture: Obligate intracellular parasite that cannot grow on cell-free media; requires McCoy cell monolayer culture; NAAT on first-catch urine or vaginal swab is standard of care.
vignette: A 22-year-old sexually active woman presents with mild mucopurulent cervical discharge, cervical motion tenderness, and irregular postcoital spotting; her partner reports watery urethral discharge and painful unilateral knee arthritis.
virulence: Unique biphasic life cycle: Elementary body (EB) is infectious and survives extracellularly; Reticulate body (RB) replicates intracellularly via binary fission; lacks typical peptidoglycan muramic acid.
transmission: Sexual contact; perinatal transmission during delivery (neonatal staccato cough pneumonia and inclusion conjunctivitis).
buzzwords: Elementary body (infectious) vs Reticulate body (replicates), NAAT first-catch urine, #1 bacterial STI worldwide, Reactive arthritis triad (can't see, can't pee, can't climb a tree), Lymphogranuloma venereum (LGV L1-L3).
chiefComplaint: A 22-year-old sexually active woman presents with abnormal cervical discharge.

name: Bordetella pertussis
keyTest: Bordet-Gengou / Regan-Lowe agar ('mercury drops'), Pertussis PCR, Marked lymphocytosis
firstLineRx: Azithromycin / Clarithromycin (Macrolide prophylaxis for all close household contacts)
smear: Extremely small, ovoid, faintly staining Gram-negative coccobacilli arranged singly or in small clusters.
culture: Specialized Bordet-Gengou (potato-glycerol-blood) or Regan-Lowe charcoal-horse blood medium; produces small, shiny, glistening silver-gray colonies resembling 'mercury droplets' or split pearls.
vignette: An unvaccinated 4-year-old child experiences 2 weeks of catarrhal rhinorrhea followed by severe paroxysms of 20 consecutive hacking coughs terminating in a high-pitched inspiratory gasp and post-tussive emesis; WBC is 45,000/µL with 80% lymphocytes.
virulence: Pertussis toxin ADP-ribosylates Gi alpha, permanently turning off Gi and increasing cAMP; Tracheal cytotoxin destroys ciliated epithelial cells; Filamentous hemagglutinin (FHA) mediates epithelial tethering.
transmission: Airborne respiratory droplets; highly contagious in catarrhal phase.
buzzwords: 100-day cough, Inspiratory whoop & post-tussive vomiting, Bordet-Gengou mercury droplet colonies, Marked lymphocytosis with leukemoid reaction, Gi protein inhibition via ADP-ribosylation.
chiefComplaint: An unvaccinated 4-year-old child experiences paroxysms of severe repetitive coughing.

name: Francisella tularensis
keyTest: Requires Cysteine (BCYE or Chocolate agar), Serum agglutination titers, Tier 1 Select Agent precautions
tropism: Skin, Reticuloendothelial (Regional Lymph Nodes, Spleen), Lungs
firstLineRx: Streptomycin or Gentamicin / Doxycycline
smear: Minute, pleomorphic, faintly counterstaining Gram-negative coccobacilli that are near the resolution limit of standard light microscopy.
culture: Strictly requires cysteine for growth; dangerous laboratory biohazard (easily aerosolized with low infectious dose <10 organisms); requires biosafety level 3 (BSL-3).
vignette: A hunter who skinned wild rabbits in Arkansas develops an ulcerated erythematous papule with a punched-out base on his index finger, followed by painful suppurative axillary lymphadenopathy and 40°C fever.
virulence: Facultative intracellular bacterium that escapes macrophage phagosome into host cytoplasm; lipid-rich capsule inhibits complement-mediated lysis; extremely low infectious dose.
transmission: Direct contact with infected animal tissues (rabbits, rodents), bites from Dermacentor dog ticks or deer flies (Chrysops), ingestion of undercooked game meat, or aerosol inhalation.
buzzwords: Punched-out skin ulcer + tender regional bubo, Rabbit hunter / skinning, Requires cysteine for growth, Dermacentor tick / deer fly vector, Potential aerosol bioterror agent.
chiefComplaint: A 46-year-old hunter presents with an ulcerated finger lesion.

name: Candida albicans
keyTest: Germ tube test (+) at 37°C in serum, True hyphae & pseudohyphae, Chlamydospores at 20°C
tropism: Oral Cavity, Genital Tract (Vagina), Skin Folds, Bloodstream (Central Lines)
firstLineRx: Fluconazole (Oral/Vaginal); Echinocandin (Caspofungin / Micafungin) for invasive candidemia
smear: Gram stain demonstrates strongly Gram-positive ovoid budding yeast cells (blastoconidia) with elongated pseudohyphae; incubation in human serum at 37°C for 3 hours produces diagnostic germ tubes (parallel-walled outgrowths without constrictions).
culture: Grows rapidly on Sabouraud dextrose agar yielding creamy, convex, white colonies with distinct yeasty bread odor; green colonies on CHROMagar Candida.
vignette: A 28-year-old asthmatic patient who uses an inhaled fluticasone inhaler without a spacer develops white curd-like plaques on the tongue and buccal mucosa that bleed when scraped with a tongue depressor.
virulence: Phenotypic switching between yeast (commensal) and filamentous hyphae (invasive tissue form); secreted aspartyl proteinases (Saps) and candidalysin toxin degrade host mucosal barriers.
transmission: Normal commensal flora of GI tract, skin, and female reproductive tract; opportunistically overgrows during antibiotic therapy, corticosteroid use, diabetes mellitus, or neutropenia.
buzzwords: Germ tube positive at 37°C, Scrapeable white plaques with erythema, Pseudohyphae and budding yeast, Inhaled steroid thrush, Diaper dermatitis with satellite lesions.
chiefComplaint: A 28-year-old inhaler user develops white oral mucosal plaques.

name: Aspergillus fumigatus
keyTest: Galactomannan antigen EIA, Acute 45° dichotomous branching septate hyphae, Fruiting conidial heads
tropism: Respiratory Tract (Pre-existing cavities), Sinuses, Brain (Angioinvasive in neutropenia)
firstLineRx: Voriconazole or Isavuconazole (Surgical resection for aspergilloma)
smear: Silver (GMS) or PAS stain reveals uniform septate hyphae that branch dichotomously at narrow acute angles (~45°) without yeast forms.
culture: Rapidly growing mold on Sabouraud dextrose agar with velvety, smoky gray-green powdery surface; microscopic examination shows conidiophore with vesicle bearing phialides in single row.
vignette: A 62-year-old man with a history of treated cavitary tuberculosis presents with intermittent massive hemoptysis; chest CT demonstrates a rounded, mobile gravity-dependent soft-tissue mass inside an upper-lobe cavity with a crescent of surrounding air ('air-crescent sign').
virulence: Angioinvasive properties allow hyphae to penetrate vascular endothelium causing thrombosis, infarction, and tissue necrosis; produces gliotoxin and aflatoxin (A. flavus).
transmission: Inhalation of ubiquitous airborne environmental conidia/spores from decaying compost or hospital construction sites.
buzzwords: Acute 45° angle branching septate hyphae, Aspergilloma fungus ball in pre-existing TB cavity, Air-crescent sign on CT, Allergic Bronchopulmonary Aspergillosis (ABPA) in CF/asthma, Voriconazole.
chiefComplaint: A 62-year-old man presents with recurrent episodes of coughing up blood.

name: Histoplasma capsulatum
keyTest: Urine & Serum Histoplasma antigen EIA, Giemsa stain showing yeast packed in macrophages, Tuberculate macroconidia at 25°C
firstLineRx: Itraconazole (mild/moderate); Liposomal Amphotericin B (severe disseminated disease)
smear: Wright or Giemsa-stained bone marrow or peripheral blood smear demonstrates numerous tiny, oval budding yeast cells (2–4 µm) with narrow bases packed inside host monocytes and macrophages.
culture: Thermally dimorphic: grows as white-to-brown mold with tuberculate round macroconidia at room temperature (25°C), and converts to small budding yeast phase at 37°C.
vignette: A 45-year-old spelunker who explored bat caves in Kentucky develops fever, dry cough, hepatosplenomegaly, and bilateral reticulonodular pulmonary infiltrates; urinary Histoplasma antigen test is positive.
virulence: Survives and replicates inside macrophage phagolysosomes by alkalinizing luminal pH with urease and capture of essential iron and calcium.
transmission: Inhalation of microconidia aerosolized from soil enriched with bird (starling) or bat guano along Ohio and Mississippi River valleys.
buzzwords: 'Bird or bat droppings', Ohio and Mississippi river valleys, Spelunking in caves, Yeast hiding inside macrophages (smaller than RBC), Coin lesions & calcified granulomas mimicking TB.
chiefComplaint: A 45-year-old cave explorer presents with persistent low-grade fever.

name: Neisseria gonorrhoeae
keyTest: Ferments Glucose only (NOT maltose), Oxidase (+), Thayer-Martin / NYC medium
tropism: Genitourinary Tract, Synovium (Septic Arthritis), Pharynx, Anorectum
firstLineRx: Ceftriaxone (500 mg IM single dose) + Doxycycline (to cover Chlamydia unless ruled out)
smear: Abundant polymorphonuclear leukocytes with diagnostic pairs of Gram-negative kidney-bean-shaped diplococci nestled within cytoplasm of neutrophils (intracellular).
culture: Requires selective enriched Thayer-Martin chocolate agar (vancomycin, colistin, nystatin, trimethoprim) incubated with 5% CO2; produces acid from glucose only (vs N. meningitidis which ferments maltose and glucose).
vignette: A 24-year-old male presents with acute profuse yellow-green purulent urethral discharge and intense dysuria; urethral swab demonstrates Gram-negative intracellular diplococci within polymorphonuclear leukocytes.
virulence: Pili exhibit high-frequency antigenic and phase variation (no protective immunity / recurrent infections possible); IgA protease cleaves mucosal IgA; Lipooligosaccharide (LOS) lacks O-antigen.
transmission: Sexual contact; vertical transmission during vaginal delivery causes ophthalmia neonatorum (prevented with erythromycin eye ointment).
buzzwords: Intracellular Gram-negative diplococci, Ferments Glucose only, Asymmetric migratory polyarthralgias with pustular skin lesions (DGI), Thayer-Martin chocolate agar.
chiefComplaint: A 24-year-old male presents with profuse purulent urethral discharge.

name: Clostridium botulinum
keyTest: Mouse bioassay for botulinum neurotoxin, Anaerobic spore-forming rods, Toxin neutralization test
firstLineRx: Equine Botulinum Heptavalent Antitoxin (or BabyBIG human antitoxin for infants) + Respiratory ventilatory support
smear: Gram-positive, straight rods with oval subterminal spores with tennis-racket or club appearance under strictly anaerobic conditions.
culture: Grows under strictly anaerobic conditions on egg yolk agar producing characteristic iridescent lipase-positive sheen on colony surface.
vignette: A 5-month-old infant given natural raw honey by grandparents develops severe constipation, progressive lethargy, poor sucking reflex, weak cry, ptosis, and generalized profound hypotonia ('floppy baby syndrome').
virulence: Botulinum neurotoxin (AB toxin) light chain is a zinc endopeptidase that cleaves SNARE proteins (SNAP-25, synaptobrevin), irreversibly blocking acetylcholine exocytosis from motor nerve terminals.
transmission: Ingestion of preformed heat-labile toxin in improperly canned alkaline vegetables/smoked fish (adult foodborne botulism) or ingestion of honey spores that germinate in infant intestine (infant botulism).
buzzwords: Floppy baby syndrome, Ingestion of raw honey, Cleaves SNARE proteins blocking ACh release, Descending symmetric flaccid paralysis with cranial nerve palsies, Diplopia & ptosis.
chiefComplaint: A 5-month-old infant presents with severe constipation and weak cry.

name: Clostridium tetani
keyTest: Clinical diagnosis, Anaerobic cultivation, Round terminal spores ('drumstick' morphology)
tropism: CNS (Renshaw Cells / Inhibitory Interneurons in Spinal Cord)
firstLineRx: Wound debridement + Metronidazole + Human Tetanus Immunoglobulin (HTIG) + Tetanus Toxoid Vaccine booster
smear: Slender Gram-positive bacilli with prominent spherical terminal spores giving distinctive appearance of a bass drumstick or squash racket.
culture: Strict obligate anaerobe; colonies on blood agar exhibit fine swarming film across entire surface of plate due to vigorous peritrichous flagellar motility.
vignette: An unimmunized 60-year-old farmer steps on a rusty barbed-wire nail; 8 days later he develops lockjaw (trismus), involuntary painful facial grimacing (risus sardonicus), severe back arching (opisthotonos), and violent spasms triggered by light or noise.
virulence: Tetanospasmin neurotoxin travels retrogradely along motor axons to spinal cord inhibitory interneurons (Renshaw cells), cleaving synaptobrevin to block release of inhibitory neurotransmitters GABA and glycine.
transmission: Deep puncture wounds, contaminated trauma, or unsterile umbilical cord cutting (neonatal tetanus) introducing spores from soil or animal feces.
buzzwords: Drumstick terminal spores, Risus sardonicus (sardonic smile), Trismus (lockjaw), Opisthotonos (arched back), Cleaves synaptobrevin blocking GABA and glycine release.
chiefComplaint: An unimmunized 60-year-old farmer develops painful jaw muscle stiffness.

name: Burkholderia pseudomallei
keyTest: Oxidase (+), Ashdown agar (wrinkled purple colonies), Earthy odor
firstLineRx: Ceftazidime or Meropenem (Intensive) followed by TMP-SMX (Eradication)
smear: Gram-negative straight or slightly curved bacilli with characteristic bipolar staining resembling safety pins.
culture: Wrinkled, corrugate, dry purple colonies on selective Ashdown agar with prominent earthy odor; resistant to colistin and aminoglycosides.
vignette: A 52-year-old rice farmer with poorly controlled type 2 diabetes in Thailand presents with high remittent fevers, pleuritic chest pain, and multiple microabscesses in the liver and spleen ('swiss cheese' spleen on CT).
virulence: Type III and VI secretion systems, Burkholderia lethal factor 1, cytotoxic polysaccharide capsule preventing phagocytosis.
transmission: Percutaneous inoculation through wet tropical soil or surface water during monsoon rains, inhalation of agricultural dust.
buzzwords: Southeast Asia / Northern Australia rice paddy worker, Safety-pin bipolar Gram-negative rod, Ashdown agar wrinkled colonies, Swiss cheese spleen microabscesses.
chiefComplaint: A 52-year-old diabetic farmer presents with persistent high-spiking fevers.

name: Talaromyces marneffei
keyTest: Thermal dimorphism (25°C mold with soluble red pigment; 37°C intracellular fission yeast)
tropism: Skin & Soft Tissue, Reticuloendothelial System, Lungs
firstLineRx: Amphotericin B (Induction) followed by Itraconazole (Maintenance)
smear: Wright-Giemsa or GMS stain shows small oval intracellular yeast cells (2-4 µm) dividing by binary fission with a clear transverse cross-wall (septum), unlike budding yeasts.
culture: On Sabouraud dextrose agar at 25°C, grows as bluish-green mold that diffuses a characteristic deep brick-red soluble pigment into the reverse of the agar; converts to yeast phase at 37°C.
vignette: A 36-year-old HIV patient with CD4 count of 28 cells/µL returning from Chiang Mai, Thailand presents with high fever, generalized lymphadenopathy, hepatosplenomegaly, and dozens of molluscum-like umbilicated skin papules on the face and neck.
virulence: Intracellular survival within macrophages, heat-shock proteins, cell-wall melanin conferring resistance to oxidative burst.
transmission: Inhalation of fungal conidia from endemic soil or aerosolized from bamboo rat burrows in Southeast Asia.
buzzwords: Southeast Asia / Thailand AIDS indicator, Diffuse red pigment on agar at 25°C, Intracellular yeast dividing by fission (cross-wall), Umbilicated facial papules.
chiefComplaint: A 36-year-old immunocompromised traveler presents with multiple umbilicated facial skin papules.

name: Streptococcus agalactiae
keyTest: Catalase (-), CAMP test (+), Hippurate hydrolysis (+), Bacitracin resistant
firstLineRx: Intrapartum IV Penicillin G or Ampicillin (or Cefazolin / Clindamycin if allergic)
smear: Gram-positive spherical to ovoid cocci arranged in short to medium chains.
culture: Narrow zone of beta-hemolysis on sheep blood agar; forms arrow-shaped arrowhead zone of synergistic hemolysis when streaked perpendicular to S. aureus (CAMP test); hydrolyzes sodium hippurate.
vignette: A 2-day-old infant born to an unscreened mother presents with lethargy, hypothermia, tachypnea, grunting, and bulging fontanelle; CSF reveals elevated neutrophils and Gram-positive diplococci in chains.
virulence: Polysaccharide capsule (sialic acid rich) inhibits complement deposition; Beta-hemolysin/cytolysin.
transmission: Vertical transmission during passage through colonized maternal vaginal canal; universal prenatal screening performed at 36-37 weeks gestation.
buzzwords: CAMP test arrowhead hemolysis, Hippurate hydrolysis (+), #1 cause of neonatal meningitis and sepsis, Universal screening at 36-37 weeks.
chiefComplaint: A 2-day-old newborn infant develops marked respiratory distress.

name: Streptococcus mutans / mitis (Viridans group)
keyTest: Catalase (-), Optochin resistant (no zone of inhibition), Bile insoluble, α-hemolytic
firstLineRx: IV Penicillin G or Ceftriaxone (often combined with Gentamicin)
smear: Gram-positive cocci in chains and pairs; normal oral flora.
culture: Greenish alpha-hemolysis on blood agar; insoluble in 10% bile salts and resistant to ethylhydrocupreine (optochin P-disk).
vignette: A 45-year-old woman with a history of rheumatic mitral valve prolapse presents with low-grade afternoon fevers, night sweats, splinter hemorrhages beneath her fingernails, and a worsening holosystolic murmur 3 weeks after dental cleaning.
virulence: Produces extracellular dextrans from dietary sucrose, allowing tenacious adherence to fibrin-platelet aggregates on damaged heart valves.
transmission: Transient bacteremia following dental manipulation, vigorous flossing, or oral trauma.
buzzwords: Subacute bacterial endocarditis (SBE) on previously damaged heart valve post-dental work, Dextran synthesis from sucrose, Optochin resistant, Bile insoluble.
chiefComplaint: A 45-year-old female presents with low-grade daily afternoon fevers.

name: Enterococcus faecalis
keyTest: Catalase (-), Bile esculin (+ black slant), Grows in 6.5% NaCl, PYR (+)
tropism: Urinary Tract, Heart Valves, Biliary Tract
firstLineRx: Ampicillin + Ceftriaxone (or Daptomycin / Linezolid for VRE)
smear: Gram-positive oval cocci in pairs and short chains, often morphologically indistinguishable from S. pneumoniae on smear.
culture: Hydrolyzes esculin in the presence of 40% bile to produce dark black ferric precipitate; thrives in harsh 6.5% NaCl broth; PYR (pyrrolidonyl arylamidase) positive.
vignette: A 68-year-old man who underwent transurethral resection of the prostate (TURP) develops dysuria, persistent bacteremia, and a new aortic diastolic murmur; blood cultures grow bile-esculin positive Gram-positive cocci.
virulence: Inherent resistance to many cephalosporins and aminoglycosides; vanA/vanB gene operon alters D-Ala-D-Ala to D-Ala-D-Lac preventing vancomycin binding.
transmission: Normal bowel flora; hospital-acquired instrumentation (urinary Foley catheters, cystoscopy, central lines).
buzzwords: Bile esculin black agar, 6.5% NaCl tolerance, Post-GU/GI procedure endocarditis, VanA gene D-Ala-D-Lac alteration (VRE).
chiefComplaint: A 68-year-old hospitalized man develops burning pain during urination.

name: Staphylococcus epidermidis
keyTest: Catalase (+), Coagulase (-), Novobiocin sensitive, Urease (+)
tropism: Prosthetic Implants, Catheters, Artificial Heart Valves
firstLineRx: Vancomycin + Rifampin (for biofilm penetration)
smear: Gram-positive round cocci arranged in clusters; predominant normal skin commensal.
culture: White porcelain non-pigmented colonies without hemolysis on sheep blood agar; growth inhibited by novobiocin disk (>16 mm zone).
vignette: A 60-year-old man who received a prosthetic knee replacement 6 months ago presents with insidious, progressive knee pain, localized swelling, and joint effusion without systemic septic shock.
virulence: Extracellular polysaccharide slime (glycocalyx) synthesis enabling multilayered biofilm formation on artificial biomaterials.
transmission: Normal skin flora; contamination of indwelling intravascular catheters, prosthetic joint hardware, or ventriculoperitoneal shunts.
buzzwords: Prosthetic valve/joint biofilm, Novobiocin sensitive, Coagulase negative, Glycocalyx slime.
chiefComplaint: A 60-year-old prosthetic knee recipient develops persistent localized joint pain.

name: Staphylococcus saprophyticus
keyTest: Catalase (+), Coagulase (-), Novobiocin resistant, Urease (+)
firstLineRx: TMP-SMX (Trimethoprim-Sulfamethoxazole) or Nitrofurantoin
smear: Gram-positive spherical cocci in small irregular clusters.
culture: White or yellow non-hemolytic colonies; grows right up to the novobiocin disk with no significant zone of inhibition (<16 mm, novobiocin resistant).
vignette: A 20-year-old college student presents with a 2-day history of intense burning on urination, urinary frequency, and suprapubic tenderness 3 days after returning from a weekend trip with her new partner.
virulence: Urease enzyme production and surface uro-adhesins specifically targeting uroepithelial cell glycolipids.
transmission: Normal flora of the female genital tract and perineum; mechanical inoculation into urethra during sexual intercourse.
buzzwords: #2 cause of uncomplicated UTI in young sexually active females (honeymoon cystitis), Novobiocin resistant, Coagulase negative.
chiefComplaint: A 20-year-old sexually active female presents with intense painful urination.

name: Clostridium perfringens
keyTest: Nagler reaction (+), Double zone of hemolysis on blood agar, Catalase (-)
tropism: Skeletal Muscle, Subcutaneous Soft Tissue, Gastrointestinal Tract
firstLineRx: IV High-dose Penicillin G + Clindamycin (for toxin suppression) + Emergent surgical debridement
smear: Large, boxcar-shaped Gram-positive bacilli with blunt square ends; notably lacks polymorphonuclear neutrophils due to leukocidin lysis.
culture: Rapid anaerobic growth displaying a distinctive double zone of hemolysis on blood agar (inner complete theta-hemolysis, outer partial alpha-hemolysis); Nagler egg yolk agar confirms lecithinase inhibition.
vignette: A 38-year-old motorcycle accident victim with an open compound tibia fracture develops sudden, agonizing leg pain out of proportion to exam, bronze discoloration of the skin, and crackling crepitus upon palpation.
virulence: Alpha toxin (phospholipase C / lecithinase) cleaves cell membrane phospholipids causing massive myonecrosis, hemolysis, and vascular collapse; Enterotoxin causes late-onset food poisoning.
transmission: Contamination of deep traumatic puncture wounds with soil spores; consumption of reheated meat dishes.
buzzwords: Gas gangrene / Clostridial myonecrosis, Alpha toxin lecithinase, Double zone of hemolysis, Boxcar rod, Tissue crepitus.
chiefComplaint: A 38-year-old trauma patient develops severe excruciating leg pain.

name: Corynebacterium diphtheriae

morphology.shape: Club-shaped rod in Chinese letter / palisade arrangements

keyTest: Cystine-tellurite agar (black colonies), Loeffler's serum (metachromatic granules), Elek test (+)
firstLineRx: Diphtheria Antitoxin (Equine DAT) + Erythromycin or Penicillin G
smear: Pleomorphic Gram-positive club-shaped non-spore-forming bacilli arranged in V- or L-shapes resembling Chinese calligraphy characters; Albert or Neisser stain demonstrates reddish-purple volutin (polyphosphate) metachromatic granules.
culture: Forms gunmetal black/gray colonies on cystine-tellurite blood agar; grows rapidly on Loeffler's coagulated serum medium; Elek in vitro immunodiffusion test confirms toxigenicity.
vignette: A 6-year-old immigrant child whose parents declined vaccination presents with low-grade fever, sore throat, cervical lymphadenopathy producing a 'bull neck' appearance, and a tough, gray pseudomembrane over the posterior tonsils that bleeds profusely upon attempted dislodgement.
virulence: Diphtheria A-B exotoxin (encoded by beta-prophage); the A subunit catalyzes ADP-ribosylation of elongation factor 2 (EF-2), completely terminating host cell protein synthesis.
transmission: Airborne respiratory droplets from actively infected individuals or asymptomatic nasopharyngeal carriers.
buzzwords: Pseudomembranous pharyngitis that bleeds on scraping, Bull neck lymphadenopathy, ADP-ribosylation of EF-2, Tellurite black colonies, Metachromatic granules.
chiefComplaint: A 6-year-old unimmunized child presents with severe sore throat.

name: Nocardia asteroides
keyTest: Modified Kinyoun acid-fast (+), Catalase (+), Urease (+), Aerobic growth
tropism: Lungs, Central Nervous System (Brain Abscess), Skin
firstLineRx: Trimethoprim-Sulfamethoxazole (TMP-SMX) (high dose, prolonged) ± Carbapenem / Amikacin
smear: Gram-positive, thin, beaded, delicate branching filaments that stain positively with modified acid-fast (Fite-Faraco / weak sulfuric acid decolorizer) staining.
culture: Strict aerobe with dry, chalky-white to orange wrinkled colonies on non-selective media, emitting an earthy soil odor; takes 3 to 7 days to grow.
vignette: A 55-year-old man on chronic high-dose prednisone for a kidney transplant presents with subacute fever, cough with purulent sputum, and weight loss; chest CT reveals multiple cavitary nodular infiltrates, and brain MRI shows multiple ring-enhancing lesions.
virulence: Mycolic acids in cell wall resist phagosomal digestion; produces superoxide dismutase and catalase to inactivate neutrophil oxidative burst.
transmission: Inhalation of soil saprophytes (pulmonary); direct cutaneous inoculation (mycetoma).
buzzwords: Branching beaded filaments, Weakly/partially acid-fast, Cavitary pulmonary nodules + Brain abscess in immunocompromised host, TMP-SMX treatment.
chiefComplaint: A 55-year-old renal transplant patient presents with a persistent productive cough.

name: Actinomyces israelii
keyTest: Acid-fast negative, Sulfur granules in pus, Molar tooth colonies on agar
tropism: Cervicofacial Soft Tissue, Mandible, Abdomen & Pelvis
firstLineRx: High-dose IV Penicillin G (2-6 weeks) followed by Oral Penicillin V (6-12 months)
smear: Gram-positive branching filamentous bacteria embedded in amorphous proteinaceous debris forming macroscopic hard yellow 'sulfur granules'; NOT acid-fast.
culture: Slow-growing obligate anaerobe requiring 7 to 14 days; produces white, rough, wrinkled 'molar tooth' colonies on brain-heart infusion agar.
vignette: A 42-year-old male presents with a slowly enlarging, hard, non-tender lump along the angle of his lower jaw 2 months after an uncomplicated dental tooth extraction; the lesion breaks through the skin via multiple draining sinus tracts discharging gritty yellow granules.
virulence: Low intrinsic virulence; forms chronic destructive granulomatous lesions with dense fibrotic scar tissue across tissue planes ignoring normal fascial boundaries.
transmission: Endogenous normal commensal of the oral cavity, gingival crevices, and tonsillar crypts; invasive disease requires mucosal barrier disruption (dental surgery, IUD placement).
buzzwords: Cervicofacial lumpy jaw, Draining sinus tracts across fascial planes, Yellow sulfur granules, Molar tooth colonies, High-dose prolonged Penicillin.
chiefComplaint: A 42-year-old male presents with a slowly growing non-tender jaw mass.

name: Klebsiella pneumoniae
keyTest: MacConkey agar (pink mucoid colonies), Urease (+), Indole (-), Non-motile
tropism: Lungs (Upper Lobes), Urinary Tract, Biliary Tree
firstLineRx: 3rd/4th Gen Cephalosporin (Ceftriaxone / Cefepime) or Carbapenem (if ESBL producer)
smear: Short, plump Gram-negative bacilli surrounded by a prominent unstained gelatinous capsule halo.
culture: Ferments lactose vigorously on MacConkey agar yielding large, hyper-mucoid, glistening pink colonies with a string-test positive viscosity; non-motile.
vignette: A 58-year-old chronic alcoholic male presents with sudden high fever, shaking chills, and a cough productive of gelatinous, dark-red 'currant jelly' sputum; chest radiograph demonstrates right upper lobe consolidation with a prominent bulging interlobar fissure.
virulence: Abundant polysaccharide capsule (K antigen) prevents phagocytosis; lipopolysaccharide endotoxin causes septic shock; frequent plasmid carriage of extended-spectrum beta-lactamases (ESBL) and carbapenemases (KPC).
transmission: Aspiration of colonized oropharyngeal secretions in alcoholics, diabetics, or nursing home residents; contaminated hospital ventilators.
buzzwords: Currant jelly sputum, Bulging interlobar fissure on CXR, Alcoholics and diabetics, Mucoid lactose fermenter, Non-motile Gram-negative rod.
chiefComplaint: A 58-year-old alcoholic male presents with a productive cough of thick sputum.

name: Proteus mirabilis
keyTest: Urease strongly (+), Swarming motility on sheep blood agar, MacConkey (colorless, non-lactose fermenter), H2S (+)
firstLineRx: Ceftriaxone, Ciprofloxacin, or TMP-SMX
smear: Gram-negative pleomorphic bacilli with extensive peritrichous flagella.
culture: Exhibits dramatic periodic waves of 'swarming motility' forming concentric rings over non-inhibitory blood agar; non-lactose fermenter on MacConkey agar; rapidly hydrolyzes urea producing deep pink slant within minutes.
vignette: A 64-year-old woman with recurrent urinary tract infections presents with severe right flank pain and hematuria; urinalysis reveals an alkaline pH of 8.5, and non-contrast CT abdomen shows a large, radio-opaque staghorn calculus occupying the entire renal pelvis.
virulence: Potent urease enzyme hydrolyzes urea into carbon dioxide and ammonia, markedly raising urine pH (>8.0) and precipitating magnesium ammonium phosphate (struvite) stones.
transmission: Ascending infection from colonized perineum or long-term indwelling Foley catheters.
buzzwords: Swarming motility on blood agar, Alkaline urine (pH > 8.0), Struvite staghorn renal calculi (magnesium ammonium phosphate), Highly urease-positive.
chiefComplaint: A 64-year-old woman presents with severe unilateral flank pain.

name: Shigella dysenteriae
keyTest: MacConkey (colorless, non-lactose fermenter), Hektoen enteric agar (green colonies, no H2S), Non-motile
firstLineRx: Azithromycin, Ciprofloxacin, or Ceftriaxone (hydration is critical)
smear: Gram-negative slender rods; microscopic fecal exam demonstrates abundant polymorphonuclear leukocytes and red blood cells.
culture: Non-lactose fermenting colorless colonies on MacConkey agar; produces green colonies on Hektoen enteric agar without black centers (unlike Salmonella, does NOT produce hydrogen sulfide); strictly non-motile.
vignette: An 8-year-old boy in daycare develops high fever, lower abdominal cramping, and 15 episodes of bloody mucoid diarrhea with painful rectal straining (tenesmus); two days later he develops pallor, oliguria, and petechiae (hemolytic uremic syndrome).
virulence: Shiga toxin (A-B toxin) cleaves 28S rRNA of the 60S eukaryotic ribosomal subunit, halting host protein synthesis and destroying microvascular endothelium; actin polymerization allows cell-to-cell spread without extracellular exposure.
transmission: Fecal-oral transmission via the four Fs (Fingers, Flies, Food, Feces); extremely low infectious dose (as few as 10 organisms survive gastric acid).
buzzwords: Low infectious dose (10-100 organisms), Shiga toxin inactivating 60S ribosome, Hemolytic Uremic Syndrome (HUS), Tenesmus with bloody mucoid stool, Non-motile no H2S.
chiefComplaint: An 8-year-old schoolchild presents with frequent painful bloody diarrhea.

name: Helicobacter pylori
keyTest: Urease strongly (+), Oxidase (+), Catalase (+), Rapid urease breath test (+)
firstLineRx: Quadruple Therapy: Bismuth subsalicylate + Metronidazole + Tetracycline + Proton Pump Inhibitor (PPI)
smear: Gram-negative, curved, spiral or seagull-shaped rod with multiple unipolar lophotrichous flagella; visualized in gastric antral biopsies with Warthin-Starry or Giemsa silver stains.
culture: Fastidious microaerophilic organism requiring blood-supplemented media at 37°C for 3 to 5 days; diagnosed clinically via 13C-urea breath test, stool antigen, or mucosal biopsy rapid urease (CLO) test.
vignette: A 47-year-old male executive presents with months of gnawing, burning epigastric abdominal pain that improves temporarily after eating meals and worsens 2 hours postprandially; endoscopy reveals a solitary 1.5-cm duodenal bulb peptic ulcer.
virulence: Urease produces alkaline ammonia cloud neutralizing gastric acid; CagA (cytotoxin-associated gene A) and VacA (vacuolating cytotoxin) induce mucosal inflammation and chronic atrophic gastritis.
transmission: Human-to-human transmission via fecal-oral or oral-oral routes during childhood.
buzzwords: Urea breath test, Urease-producing curved rod, Duodenal and gastric peptic ulcers, Gastric adenocarcinoma, MALT lymphoma.
chiefComplaint: A 47-year-old male presents with gnawing epigastric abdominal pain.

name: Bartonella henselae
keyTest: Warthin-Starry silver stain (+), Serology (IFA), Difficult to culture (>21 days)
tropism: Lymph Nodes, Vascular Endothelium (AIDS), Liver & Spleen
firstLineRx: Azithromycin (Cat Scratch Disease) or Doxycycline (Bacillary Angiomatosis / Peliosis)
smear: Small, pleomorphic, fastidious Gram-negative bacilli that stain poorly on standard Gram stain; readily visualized using Warthin-Starry silver impregnation stain in infected lymph node tissue.
culture: Extremely slow growing; requires enriched chocolate or rabbit blood agar incubated in 5% CO2 for up to 3 to 4 weeks.
vignette: A 9-year-old boy presents with a single, firm, non-tender red papule on his right forearm followed 3 weeks later by painful, suppurative axillary lymphadenopathy; his family adopted a stray kitten 1 month earlier.
virulence: BadA adhesin promotes binding to endothelial cells and fibronectin, triggering vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) secretion and robust vascular proliferation (angiomatosis).
transmission: Scratches, bites, or saliva contamination from domestic kittens infested with the cat flea (Ctenocephalides felis).
buzzwords: Cat scratch disease with regional axillary lymphadenopathy, Bacillary angiomatosis in HIV/AIDS, Warthin-Starry silver stain, Kitten exposure.
chiefComplaint: A 9-year-old child presents with a swollen tender armpit lymph node.

name: Brucella melitensis
keyTest: Oxidase (+), Catalase (+), Urease (+ in minutes), Prolonged blood culture hold (Castaneda bottle)
firstLineRx: Doxycycline + Rifampin (or Gentamicin) for 6 weeks minimum
smear: Very small, poorly staining Gram-negative coccobacilli; facultative intracellular pathogens inside host macrophages.
culture: Requires prolonged incubation in specialized biphasic Castaneda blood culture bottles for up to 4 weeks; small, translucent colonies that hydrolyze urea rapidly within 15 minutes.
vignette: A 33-year-old goatherd returning from the Mediterranean region presents with fluctuating daily remittent fevers with drenching night sweats emitting a peculiar moldy odor, profound fatigue, and sacroiliitis after consuming artisanal unpasteurized goat cheese.
virulence: Smooth lipopolysaccharide (O-polysaccharide) prevents phagolysosomal fusion inside macrophages; forms non-caseating granulomas throughout the reticuloendothelial system.
transmission: Ingestion of unpasteurized goat, sheep, or cow dairy products; direct contact with aborted animal placentas through broken skin; laboratory aerosol exposure.
buzzwords: Undulant fever (Malta fever), Unpasteurized goat cheese/dairy, Sacroiliitis, Facultative intracellular inside reticuloendothelial system, Doxycycline + Rifampin.
chiefComplaint: A 33-year-old dairy worker presents with fluctuating undulating fevers.

name: Pasteurella multocida
keyTest: Oxidase (+), Catalase (+), Indole (+), Mouse-like odor, No growth on MacConkey agar
tropism: Skin & Soft Tissue, Periosteum & Joint Space
firstLineRx: Amoxicillin-Clavulanate (Augmentin) (or Doxycycline if penicillin-allergic)
smear: Small, oval Gram-negative coccobacillus demonstrating distinctive bipolar staining ('safety-pin' appearance with darker stained poles on Giemsa or methylene blue stain).
culture: Grows well on sheep blood and chocolate agar producing grayish, smooth, non-hemolytic colonies with a characteristic musty, mouse-like odor; does NOT grow on MacConkey agar (differentiates from Enterobacteriaceae).
vignette: A 30-year-old veterinarian presents with severe, throbbing pain, erythema, and purulent drainage from a puncture wound on her right index finger only 8 hours after being bitten by a domestic cat.
virulence: Pasteurella multocida toxin (PMT) activates intracellular G-proteins, stimulating cell proliferation and bone resorption; antiphagocytic hyaluronic acid capsule.
transmission: Animal bites, scratches, or licking of broken skin by domestic cats (70-90% carriage) or dogs (50% carriage).
buzzwords: Cat and dog bites, Rapid onset cellulitis within 24 hours, Bipolar safety-pin staining, Mouse-like odor, Amoxicillin-clavulanate first line.
chiefComplaint: A 30-year-old woman develops rapidly spreading redness and swelling on her hand.

name: Rickettsia rickettsii
keyTest: Weil-Felix reaction (+ cross-reaction with Proteus vulgaris), Serology (IFA), Biopsy with direct immunofluorescence
firstLineRx: Doxycycline (immediate empiric therapy, even in children)
smear: Extremely small, obligate intracellular Gram-negative bacterium; does not stain well with Gram stain; visualized inside host vascular endothelial cells using Giemsa stain.
culture: Cannot grow on cell-free artificial agar; requires living tissue cell cultures or embryonated eggs.
vignette: A 16-year-old boy returning from a summer camping trip in North Carolina develops sudden onset of 40°C fever, severe frontal headache, and myalgias, followed on day 4 by a blanching macular rash that began on his wrists and ankles and spread inward to his trunk, palms, and soles.
virulence: Invades and replicates within vascular endothelial cells, causing widespread necrotizing vasculitis, microvascular leakage, non-cardiogenic pulmonary edema, and multi-organ failure.
transmission: Bite of the American dog tick (Dermacentor variabilis) or Rocky Mountain wood tick (Dermacentor andersoni); endemic in the southeastern US.
buzzwords: Rocky Mountain Spotted Fever, Dermacentor dog tick, Rash starts on wrists/ankles and spreads centripetally to palms and soles, Vasculitis, Doxycycline.
chiefComplaint: A 16-year-old camper presents with high fever and sudden severe headache.

name: Coxiella burnetii
keyTest: Phase I and Phase II antibody serology (IFA), Negative blood cultures (culture-negative endocarditis)
firstLineRx: Doxycycline (Acute Q fever) or Doxycycline + Hydroxychloroquine (Chronic endocarditis)
smear: Small pleomorphic rod living inside host phagolysosomes; forms a specialized spore-like small cell variant that resists heat and desiccation in the environment.
