culture: Obligate intracellular pathogen; highly infectious (BSL-3 agent); routine blood cultures are negative; diagnosis confirmed by Phase I and Phase II IgG/IgM titers.
vignette: A 39-year-old livestock veterinarian who recently assisted with sheep birthing presents with sudden high fever, drenching sweats, severe retro-orbital headache, and dry cough; chest X-ray shows patchy consolidation, and cardiac exam reveals a new murmur in a prosthetic valve with negative routine blood cultures.
virulence: Spore-like small cell variant survives months in soil; lipopolysaccharide antigenic phase variation (Phase II in acute disease, Phase I in chronic disease).
transmission: Inhalation of desiccated aerosols from amniotic fluid, placenta, or milk of infected sheep, goats, or cattle; no arthropod vector required.
buzzwords: Q fever, Inhalation of sheep/cattle placental aerosols, Culture-negative endocarditis, No rash, Phase I and Phase II antibodies, Spore-like resistance.
chiefComplaint: A 39-year-old livestock veterinarian presents with sudden onset of high fever and chills.

name: Human gammaherpesvirus 4 (Epstein-Barr virus)
keyTest: Heterophile antibody Monospot (+), Atypical Downey lymphocytes (>10% on peripheral smear), Viral capsid antigen (VCA) IgM (+)
firstLineRx: Supportive care (avoid contact sports to prevent splenic rupture; avoid ampicillin/amoxicillin which triggers maculopapular rash)
smear: Peripheral blood smear demonstrates reactive atypical CD8+ cytotoxic T lymphocytes ('Downey cells') with abundant vacuolated basophilic cytoplasm that molds around neighboring red blood cells.
culture: Viral cell culture rarely performed; diagnosed via Paul-Bunnell heterophile agglutination (Monospot test) or anti-EBV serology (anti-VCA, anti-EBNA).
vignette: A 19-year-old college student presents with profound fatigue, 39°C fever, severe exudative pharyngitis, posterior cervical lymphadenopathy, and mild splenomegaly; administration of amoxicillin by an urgent care clinic resulted in a diffuse pruritic maculopapular rash.
virulence: Envelope glycoprotein gp350 binds complement receptor 2 (CR2 / CD21) on human B lymphocytes; latent membrane proteins (LMP-1) mimic CD40 signaling driving B cell proliferation.
transmission: Salivary transmission via close oral contact ('kissing disease') among adolescents and young adults.
buzzwords: Infectious mononucleosis, Heterophile antibodies (Monospot), Atypical reactive CD8+ T cells (Downey cells), CD21 B-cell receptor, Ampicillin-induced rash, Burkitt lymphoma.
chiefComplaint: A 19-year-old college student presents with profound fatigue and painful sore throat.

name: Human betaherpesvirus 5 (Cytomegalovirus)
keyTest: Owl-eye basophilic intranuclear inclusion bodies on biopsy, Heterophile antibody negative (Monospot -), PCR viral load
tropism: Monocytes, Endothelial Cells, Retina, Gastrointestinal Tract
firstLineRx: Ganciclovir / Valganciclovir (or Foscarnet / Cidofovir for resistant strains)
smear: Histopathology shows massive cytomegaly with prominent basophilic intranuclear inclusion bodies surrounded by a clear halo ('owl's-eye inclusions').
culture: Human fibroblast shell-vial culture demonstrates rapid viral antigen detection; quantitative plasma PCR is primary diagnostic modality.
vignette: A 35-year-old AIDS patient with a CD4 count of 35 cells/µL presents with progressive painless blurring of vision, visual floaters, and photopsia; funduscopic examination reveals extensive full-thickness retinal hemorrhages with yellow-white granular exudates along retinal vessels ('pizza pie retinopathy').
virulence: Latency in monocytes and bone marrow myeloid progenitors; downregulation of MHC Class I molecules allowing evasion of CD8+ cytotoxic T lymphocytes.
transmission: Saliva, breast milk, sexual contact, blood transfusion, organ transplantation, and transplacental mother-to-fetus transmission.
buzzwords: Owl-eye intranuclear inclusion bodies, Monospot-negative mononucleosis, Pizza-pie retinitis in AIDS (CD4 < 50), #1 congenital viral infection with sensorineural hearing loss.
chiefComplaint: A 35-year-old immunocompromised male presents with painless blurred vision and floaters.

name: Human alphaherpesvirus 3 (Varicella-zoster virus)
keyTest: Tzanck smear (multinucleated giant cells), PCR of vesicle fluid, Direct fluorescent antibody (DFA)
tropism: Dorsal Root & Trigeminal Ganglia, Skin Epidermis
firstLineRx: Valacyclovir, Famciclovir, or IV Acyclovir (supportive for healthy children)
smear: Tzanck smear scraping of the vesicle base reveals multinucleated giant cells and Cowdry A eosinophilic intranuclear inclusions.
culture: Viral culture or PCR of vesicular fluid demonstrates VZV DNA; serology confirms acute varicella or reactivation.
vignette: A 62-year-old woman presents with severe, burning, stabbing pain across the right side of her chest, followed 3 days later by an eruption of clustered erythematous vesicles strictly restricted to the right T5 dermatome that does not cross the midline.
virulence: Establishes lifelong latent infection in the sensory dorsal root ganglia and cranial nerve ganglia (trigeminal / geniculate ganglia); reactivates during periods of waning cellular immunity.
transmission: Respiratory droplets or direct contact with fluid from active vesicular skin lesions.
buzzwords: Dermatomal shingles (herpes zoster), Dewdrops on a rose petal vesicles in all stages of development, Dorsal root ganglion latency, Postherpetic neuralgia, Tzanck smear.
chiefComplaint: A 62-year-old woman presents with severe burning pain along her left chest wall.

name: Hepatitis B virus
keyTest: HBsAg (+ active infection), HBeAg (+ high viral infectivity), Anti-HBc IgM (+ window period / acute)
firstLineRx: Entecavir or Tenofovir (oral reverse-transcriptase inhibitors) or PEG-Interferon alpha
smear: Liver biopsy reveals 'ground-glass hepatocytes' caused by cytoplasm densely packed with Hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg).
culture: Cannot be cultured in routine microbiological media; diagnosed by serologic panel (HBsAg, anti-HBs, anti-HBc, HBeAg) and serum HBV DNA PCR.
vignette: A 27-year-old male presents with fatigue, nausea, dark tea-colored urine, and right upper quadrant discomfort preceded by 2 weeks of fever, hives (urticaria), and polyarthritis (serum sickness-like prodrome); physical exam reveals scleral icterus and tender hepatomegaly.
virulence: Partially double-stranded circular DNA genome that replicates via an RNA intermediate using viral reverse transcriptase; Integration into host genome increases risk of hepatocellular carcinoma even without cirrhosis.
transmission: Parenteral (IV drug use, needle sticks), sexual intercourse, and vertical mother-to-child transmission during delivery.
buzzwords: Ground-glass hepatocytes, Serum sickness prodrome (fever, urticaria, arthritis), Dane particle, HBsAg and anti-HBc IgM in acute window period, Polyarteritis nodosa association.
chiefComplaint: A 27-year-old male presents with progressive yellowing of his eyes and skin.

name: Hepacivirus C (Hepatitis C virus)
keyTest: Anti-HCV antibody (screening), Quantitative HCV RNA PCR (active infection / cure)
firstLineRx: Direct-Acting Antivirals (DAAs): Sofosbuvir-Velpatasvir or Glecaprevir-Pibrentasvir (curative >95%)
smear: Liver biopsy shows lymphoid aggregates in portal tracts, focal macrovesicular steatosis, and progressive bridging fibrosis leading to cirrhosis.
culture: Cannot be propagated in conventional cell culture; diagnosed via serologic screening for anti-HCV followed by confirmatory plasma HCV RNA RT-PCR.
vignette: A 49-year-old man who injected drugs in his twenties presents for routine evaluation; routine blood work reveals asymptomatic elevated ALT/AST, positive anti-HCV antibodies, and detectable serum HCV RNA; physical exam demonstrates mild palmar erythema and spider angiomas.
virulence: Lacks 3'-to-5' proofreading exonuclease in its RNA-dependent RNA polymerase, causing hypervariable envelope glycoprotein (E2) mutations (quasispecies) that completely evade neutralizing antibodies.
transmission: Blood-borne transmission, predominantly via intravenous drug use, contaminated blood transfusions prior to 1992, or unsterilized tattoo needles.
buzzwords: High rate of chronic carrier state (>80%), Lack of 3'-to-5' proofreading exonuclease generating antigenic quasispecies, Mixed cryoglobulinemia, Curative Direct-Acting Antivirals.
chiefComplaint: A 49-year-old male presents with persistent generalized fatigue.

name: Measles morbillivirus
keyTest: Koplik spots on physical exam, Measles IgM serology, RT-PCR, Warthin-Finkeldey giant cells
tropism: Respiratory Epithelium, Lymphoid Tissue, Endothelial Cells
firstLineRx: Supportive care + Vitamin A supplementation (significantly reduces pediatric mortality)
smear: Histopathology of lymphoid tissue demonstrates Warthin-Finkeldey multinucleated giant cells containing eosinophilic cytoplasmic and intranuclear inclusion bodies.
culture: Diagnosed by viral RT-PCR or measles-specific serum IgM antibodies.
vignette: An unvaccinated 4-year-old child presents with a high fever (40°C), cough, coryza, and prominent photophobia with red conjunctivae; examination reveals tiny irregular red lesions with blue-white central specks on the buccal mucosa opposite the molars, followed 2 days later by a confluent maculopapular rash starting at the hairline and spreading downward.
virulence: Hemagglutinin (H protein) mediates attachment to host CD46 / CD150; Fusion (F protein) mediates cell membrane fusion and giant cell formation; induces profound prolonged immune suppression.
transmission: Extremely contagious airborne respiratory droplet nuclei that remain suspended in room air for up to 2 hours after an infected person leaves (R0 = 12-18).
buzzwords: Three C's (Cough, Coryza, Conjunctivitis), Koplik spots on buccal mucosa, Descending maculopapular rash, Subacute Sclerosing Panencephalitis (SSPE), Vitamin A treatment.
chiefComplaint: A 4-year-old unvaccinated child presents with high fever, cough, and red eyes.

name: Norwalk virus
keyTest: RT-PCR of stool or vomitus, Extreme resistance to alcohol-based hand sanitizers, Low infectious dose
firstLineRx: Oral / IV rehydration therapy (self-limiting in 24-48 hours)
smear: Small, round, non-enveloped viral particles (27-35 nm) with cup-shaped surface indentations visible on transmission electron microscopy.
culture: Cannot be routinely propagated in diagnostic cell lines; diagnosed via multiplex gastrointestinal PCR panels or viral enzyme immunoassays.
vignette: A 28-year-old cruise ship passenger develops sudden, explosive projectile vomiting, watery non-bloody diarrhea, and low-grade fever 24 hours after eating at a communal seafood buffet; over 150 other passengers and crew members develop identical symptoms within 48 hours.
virulence: Extreme environmental stability resisting freezing, heat up to 60°C, and alcohol hand sanitizers; blunts jejunal villi causing transient malabsorption.
transmission: Fecal-oral route via contaminated food (especially raw oysters), water, fomites, and aerosolized vomitus droplets; low infectious dose (<20 particles).
buzzwords: Explosive projectile vomiting on cruise ships and school dorms, Non-enveloped resistant to alcohol hand sanitizers, Watery non-bloody diarrhea, Extremely low infectious dose.
chiefComplaint: A 28-year-old cruise ship passenger develops sudden explosive vomiting.

name: Coccidioides immitis
commonName: Valley Fever / San Joaquin Valley Fungus
keyTest: KOH / Silver stain shows thick-walled spherules filled with endospores, Barrel-shaped arthroconidia on Sabouraud agar, Complement fixation serology
firstLineRx: Fluconazole or Itraconazole (Mild/Moderate) or IV Amphotericin B (Severe / Meningeal)
smear: Tissue biopsy or sputum KOH preparation reveals large (20-100 µm), thick, doubly-refractile walled spherules packed with dozens of small round endospores (2-5 µm); MUCH larger than red blood cells.
culture: At 25°C on fungal media, grows as white fluffy mold consisting of septate hyphae that fragment into highly infectious, barrel-shaped alternating arthroconidia (extreme biohazard to laboratory personnel).
vignette: A 44-year-old construction worker in Bakersfield, California presents with fever, non-productive cough, chest pain, and painful erythematous pretibial nodules on both shins (erythema nodosum) accompanied by bilateral knee arthralgias after a severe desert dust storm.
virulence: Arthroconidia enter alveoli, evade neutrophil phagocytosis, and swell into spherules that rupture to release hundreds of endospores; alkaline microenvironment production.
transmission: Inhalation of airborne arthroconidia aerosolized from alkaline desert soil in the Southwestern United States (San Joaquin Valley, Arizona, Texas).
buzzwords: Thick-walled spherules filled with endospores, Desert Southwest US / San Joaquin Valley, Erythema nodosum (desert bumps) and arthralgias (desert rheumatism), Barrel arthroconidia.
chiefComplaint: A 44-year-old construction worker in Arizona presents with persistent chest pain and cough.

name: Pneumocystis jirovecii

morphology.shape: Disc / cup-shaped cysts with central dark spot

keyTest: Grocott's methenamine silver (GMS) stain showing crushed ping-pong ball cysts, Elevated serum 1,3-beta-D-glucan, Elevated LDH
firstLineRx: Trimethoprim-Sulfamethoxazole (TMP-SMX) ± Prednisone (if PaO2 < 70 mmHg or A-a gradient > 35)
smear: Grocott's methenamine silver (GMS) or Giemsa stain of bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) fluid demonstrates cup-shaped, boat-shaped, or collapsed 'crushed ping-pong ball' cysts (5-8 µm) with central dark dot-like thickening.
culture: Cannot be cultured in vitro on artificial agar media; confirmed via silver staining, direct immunofluorescent antibody (DFA), or PCR of sputum/BAL.
vignette: A 37-year-old male with untreated HIV presents with 3 weeks of insidious, progressive exertional dyspnea, dry non-productive cough, and low-grade fever; laboratory workup reveals CD4 count of 85 cells/µL, markedly elevated LDH, and chest X-ray shows diffuse bilateral symmetrical 'batwing' ground-glass perihilar infiltrates.
virulence: Major surface glycoprotein (Msg) undergoes antigenic variation; attaches to Type I pneumocytes filling alveoli with foamy, eosinophilic honeycombed exudate.
transmission: Inhalation of airborne cysts; asymptomatic carriage is ubiquitous, but clinical disease occurs almost exclusively when CD4+ T cell counts drop below 200 cells/µL.
buzzwords: Crushed ping-pong ball / cup-shaped silver-stained cysts on BAL, CD4 < 200 in AIDS, Diffuse bilateral interstitial ground-glass batwing infiltrates, High LDH, TMP-SMX prophylaxis and treatment.

name: Trichomonas vaginalis
keyTest: Wet mount (motile trophozoites with jerky corkscrew motility), Vaginal pH > 4.5, NAAT (+)
firstLineRx: Oral Metronidazole or Tinidazole (treat BOTH patient and sexual partners)
smear: Direct saline wet mount microscopy reveals motile, pear-shaped flagellated trophozoites (10-20 µm) with four anterior flagella and an undulating membrane displaying active, jerky, corkscrew motility; NO cyst form exists.
culture: Diamond's medium can be used for culture, but nucleic acid amplification testing (NAAT) is the current gold standard diagnostic test.
vignette: A 25-year-old sexually active woman presents with profuse, foul-smelling, yellow-green frothy vaginal discharge accompanied by vulvar itching and burning; speculum examination reveals diffuse vaginal erythema with punctate hemorrhages on the cervix ('strawberry cervix'), and vaginal pH is 6.0.
virulence: Adheres to vaginal squamous epithelium via surface lipophosphoglycan and cysteine proteases; causes contact-dependent epithelial cell lysis and localized inflammatory sloughing.
transmission: Strictly sexually transmitted infection (STI); cannot survive on environmental surfaces because it exists solely as a trophozoite without a protective cyst form.
